source_refs.note: Exercise 8.2, Question 10: book p.157 (PDF 162). Answer key book p.301-302 (PDF 306-307): RHS printed 2^(n-1), correct 2^n - 1; no answer in the key. Solution book PDF 741-770 used as a reference only.

blocks.explanation:
The printed right-hand side \(2^{n-1}\) is wrong; the true value is \(2^n - 1\) (see the correction below). We prove the correct statement.
Idea: put \(x = 1\) in \((1 + x)^n\); then only the coefficients are left.
Plan: write \((1 + x)^n\), put \(x = 1\), take away \(\binom{n}{0} = 1\).
steps:
Given: the sum \(\binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots + \binom{n}{n}\).
To prove: it equals \(2^n - 1\).
Method: Binomial expansion of \((1 + x)^n\) with the special value \(x = 1\).

Expand \((1 + x)^n\)
\[(1 + x)^n = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1}x\]
\[+ \binom{n}{2}x^2 + \dots + \binom{n}{n}x^n\]
Why: Binomial theorem with first term 1; every power of 1 is 1, so each term is \(\binom{n}{r}x^r\).

Put \(x = 1\)
\[2^n = \binom{n}{0} + \binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2}\]
\[+ \dots + \binom{n}{n}\]
Why: The expansion is true for every \(x\). With \(x = 1\), \(1 + x = 2\) and every \(x^r = 1\). So the sum of all binomial coefficients is \(2^n\) (as shown in the book's deduction (iii)).

Remove the first coefficient
\[\binom{n}{0} = 1\]
\[\binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots + \binom{n}{n} = 2^n - 1\]
Why: Subtract \(\binom{n}{0} = 1\) from both sides; the required sum starts from \(\binom{n}{1}\).

Check with \(n = 3\)
\[\binom{3}{1} + \binom{3}{2} + \binom{3}{3} = 3 + 3 + 1 = 7\]
\[2^3 - 1 = 7 \;\checkmark\]
\[2^{3-1} = 4 \ne 7\]
Why: A small case confirms \(2^n - 1\) and shows that the printed \(2^{n-1}\) does not hold.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The book prints the right-hand side as \(2^{n-1}\). This is wrong for every \(n \ge 2\): for \(n = 2\), \(\binom{2}{1} + \binom{2}{2} = 3\), but \(2^{2-1} = 2\). The correct statement is \(\binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{2} + \dots + \binom{n}{n} = 2^n - 1\). (The value \(2^{n-1}\) belongs to a different sum: \(\binom{n}{1} + \binom{n}{3} + \binom{n}{5} + \dots = 2^{n-1}\), the sum of the odd-placed coefficients.) The answer key gives no answer for this question.
